title: CAD Mock Exam 3 (cross-module, 30 Q)
description: Exam-style mixed set sampled across all 9 CAD modules, core-weighted. Local practice file.

questions.prompt: On a module record, what happens if the Roles field is left blank?

choices.text: The application's roles are inherited and the module is visible to all users who have them
The module becomes hidden from absolutely everyone, including every system administrator here
Only a full system administrator account is able to see this module in the navigator at all
The module is automatically deleted

questions.explanation: If Roles is blank, the module inherits the application's roles. Populating Roles restricts the module to those specific roles.

questions.prompt: By convention, what should you pass for parm1 and parm2 in gs.eventQueue() when you don't otherwise need them?

choices.text: The literal values null and undefined, respectively, for the two parameters.
gs.getUserID() and gs.getUserName()
current.sys_id and current.number as the two parameters
Two empty strings passed as placeholders

questions.explanation: The convention is to pass gs.getUserID() as parm1 and gs.getUserName() as parm2 when those parameters aren't otherwise used. parm1/parm2 are optional string parameters.

questions.prompt: Which two client-side classes are auto-instantiated for managing forms and the current user?

choices.text: GlideRecord and GlideSystem
GlideForm (g_form) and GlideUser (g_user)
GlideAjax and GlideQuery
GlideSystem (gs) and GlideElement

questions.explanation: g_form (GlideForm) manages form fields/values and g_user (GlideUser) exposes current-user info and role checks. Both are client-side and auto-instantiated; GlideSystem (gs) is server-side.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are examples of foundation data that is shared by many different applications? (Choose 3)

choices.text: user
cmdb_ci
task
A custom application-specific table

questions.explanation: user, cmdb_ci, and task are foundation data shared by many applications. Application-specific tables are unique to a given app.

questions.prompt: When configuring a record producer, what does the Short description field control?

choices.text: The text shown in a pop-up when the user hovers over the item
The name that is displayed for the item throughout the Service Catalog
The category the item is placed into
The list of variables that appear on the form

questions.explanation: Short description is the text shown in a pop-up when a user hovers over the item. Name is the item's displayed text, Category is where it appears, and the selected variables are the form fields.

questions.prompt: Why should you choose a field's data type carefully when first creating it?

choices.text: The data type cannot be changed once any record exists.
Changing the type later can result in data loss.
The data type determines the field's column name.
Only the first field on a table is allowed to have a non-string type.

questions.explanation: Field types can be changed, but doing so after data exists can cause data loss, so the type should be chosen carefully up front. Use date/date-time fields for dates and reference/choice fields rather than free-form strings.

questions.prompt: On an application resource, what is the difference between setting the Caller Access field to Caller Tracking versus Caller Restriction?

choices.text: Caller Tracking auto-approves cross-scope calls and logs them as Allowed; Caller Restriction denies calls until they are manually approved (logged as Requested).
Caller Tracking blocks all cross-scope calls; Caller Restriction allows all cross-scope calls automatically.
Both block cross-scope calls; they differ only in whether an email notification is sent to the resource owner.
Caller Tracking applies only to REST calls, while Caller Restriction applies only to script calls.

questions.explanation: Caller Tracking automatically approves cross-scope calls and records them in the Restricted Caller Access table with a status of Allowed, giving visibility without friction. Caller Restriction denies calls by default and requires manual approval, recording them with a status of Requested until granted. The None option instead defers entirely to the resource's Accessible from setting.

questions.prompt: Which category field is used to build a hierarchy of sub-categories?

choices.text: Location
Homepage renderer
Parent
Header icon

questions.explanation: The Parent field designates a category's parent, allowing a hierarchy of sub-categories. Roles control who may order, and the various icon fields control graphics.

questions.prompt: What is the outcome of submitting a record producer (as opposed to a standard catalog item)?

choices.text: A request with requested items and catalog tasks is generated
A record is inserted into a table chosen by the developer
An approval workflow is started for the requested service
An email notification is queued for the fulfillment group

questions.explanation: A record producer inserts a record directly into a table chosen by the developer, with no request (REQ), requested items (RITM), or catalog tasks. The REQ/RITM/task outcome belongs to standard catalog items.

questions.prompt: On the client side, how do you read the sys_id of the currently logged-in user, and how does that differ from the server side?

choices.text: g_user.userID is a property on the client; gs.getUserID() is a method on the server.
g_user.getUserID() is a method on the client; gs.userID is a property on the server.
g_user.userID() is a method on both the client and the server.
gs.getUserID() works on both the client and the server.

questions.explanation: Client-side, the user's sys_id is exposed as the property g_user.userID (no parentheses). Server-side, it is returned by the method gs.getUserID(). The client identity values (userName, userID, firstName, lastName) are bare properties, while the server GlideSystem equivalents are method calls.

questions.prompt: There are several separate read ACLs for the same table and operation (for example incident.None read). What does having multiple such ACLs mean?

choices.text: Access is more locked down, because the user is now required to pass every single one of these ACLs to get in.
Each ACL is a separate case; passing any one grants access (like multiple keys for one lock).
Only the single most recently created ACL for that operation is ever actually evaluated at runtime.
The ACLs cancel each other out.

questions.explanation: Multiple ACLs for the same operation each represent a separate context in which a user might pass (OR logic). More ACLs means more ways to be granted access, not a tighter lock. This is contextual security.

questions.prompt: What does the term **artifact** refer to in the context of a scoped application?

choices.text: A deprecated, leftover application file that is no longer in use and should be deleted soon.
Any of the application files that make up an app (ACLs, business rules, tables), within its scope.
A backup copy of the application stored in the repository.
A record that exists only in the global scope.

questions.explanation: Artifacts are the application files that make up an app, living within its scope.

questions.prompt: Application files visible in an app's 'Application files' related list are records on which table?

choices.text: sys_metadata
sys_app
sys_update_xml
sys_user

questions.explanation: Application files are records on the sys_metadata table, shown filtered to the app's scope. The app record itself lives on sys_app, and update set contents live on sys_update_xml.

questions.prompt: Which roles are associated with the Automated Test Framework? (Choose 2)

choices.text: atf_test_admin
atf_test_designer
tm_test_manager
script_debugger

questions.explanation: ATF uses the atf_test_admin and atf_test_designer roles. The tm_ roles belong to Test Management, and script_debugger belongs to the Script Debugger.

questions.prompt: What is ServiceNow's default access posture, and what does it imply for new tables?

choices.text: Allow by default, so ACLs are only ever needed in order to restrict access.
Deny by default, so an ACL must grant access or it is refused.
Allow for admins only, while all other access must be explicitly scripted.
Access is determined solely by the roles set on the application menu itself.

questions.explanation: ServiceNow denies access by default; an ACL must grant it. This is why four basic CRUD ACLs are generated automatically when a table is created with a role.

questions.prompt: On a system property, what role does the Description field play when the property is exposed on a properties page?

choices.text: It becomes the property's label shown on the properties page.
It sets the default value the property uses when no value is configured.
It determines the property's data type.
It is the snake_case variable name that scripts use to reference the property's value.

questions.explanation: The Description appears as the property's label on the properties page. Without it, the property shows as an unlabeled field. The Suffix/Name (snake_case) is what scripts reference.

questions.prompt: In an email notification body, what does ${URI_REF} produce?

choices.text: The literal word LINK rendered as a hyperlink that opens the triggering record.
The record's display name as a clickable link.
The raw 32-character sys_id string of the triggering record.
The value stored in the event's parm1 parameter.

questions.explanation: ${URI_REF} renders the display name as a link to the triggering record, while ${URI} renders the word LINK. Reference-field variants (${field.URI}, ${field.URI_REF}) link to related records.

questions.prompt: Most approval workflow activities work only on which tables?

choices.text: Tables that extend the Task table
Any table in any scope
Only the global cmdb_ci table
Only tables created from scratch (not extended)

questions.explanation: All approval activities except the User Approval activity work only on tables that extend Task. The User Approval activity works with all tables. This is a key reason to extend Task when modeling assignable work.

questions.prompt: In Test Management terminology, what is a test suite?

choices.text: A repository that holds a group of test cases
A single condition checked during execution
The instance where testing will take place
The tasks describing how a feature is to be tested

questions.explanation: A test suite is a repository of test cases. A test case is a collection of related tests, a test is a collection of conditions/steps, the test environment is the instance, and a test plan describes how testing is done.

questions.prompt: Application access controls cross-scope access. To which scripts does it NOT apply?

choices.text: Scripts running in the same scope as the table.
Scripts running in the global (cross-scope) application scope on the instance.
Business rules on the table.
Any server-side script.

questions.explanation: Application access applies to all server-side scripts but does not apply to scripts executing in the same scope as the table. An app can always reach its own tables.

questions.prompt: What does the import process do when the data being imported is the same as the data already in the instance?

choices.text: It duplicates the record so both copies are kept
It skips the record
It raises a transform error and stops
It moves the existing record to an archive table

questions.explanation: The import process skips records when the incoming data matches what is already in the instance, avoiding redundant inserts or updates.

questions.prompt: Which business rule type behaves like a scheduled job, running in the background so it doesn't delay returning control to the user?

choices.text: Before
Async
Display
Query

questions.explanation: An Async Business Rule runs in parallel in the background when the server gets to it, similar to a scheduled job. It suits slow work like web-service integrations. The other four types are synchronous.

questions.prompt: On a table's Application Access tab, the "Allow access to this table via web services" option is only selectable under what condition?

choices.text: When "Accessible from" is set to All application scopes
When the table extends the Task table
When Can create and Can delete are both checked
When at least one access control rule has already been defined for the table

questions.explanation: The web services access option becomes selectable only when Accessible from is set to All application scopes; otherwise the table cannot be exposed as a web service provider.

questions.prompt: A team wants to build an application whose core feature is streaming live video with a real-time multiplayer graphics engine. Why is this a **bad** technical fit for ServiceNow?

choices.text: ServiceNow is fundamentally incapable of storing binary data such as large video files.
The data is unstructured and the app requires a graphics engine, with no clear process flow.
ServiceNow does not support JavaScript.
ServiceNow applications cannot use forms.

questions.explanation: Unstructured data + graphics engine + no process flow are all bad-fit indicators.

questions.prompt: What is a record producer?

choices.text: A special type of Service Catalog item that creates a record in a database table
A background script that periodically generates summary records
A business rule that runs after a catalog request is approved
A reporting widget that produces charts and dashboards from catalog request data over time

questions.explanation: A record producer is a special type of Service Catalog item that is an alternative to the traditional form; both create a new record in a database table. Users answer questions that populate fields on the new record.

questions.prompt: In the **baseline** configuration, what database access does one custom (scoped) application have to another custom application's table records?

choices.text: By default it has full read and write access to all of the other app's records
Read access only; no other DB operations without explicit configuration
No database access of any kind at all without explicit cross-scope configuration first
Write access only

questions.explanation: Baseline: read access to other apps' table records only; no other DB operations without explicit configuration.

questions.prompt: Which artifact provides a single location for reusable server-side functions, reducing maintenance effort?

choices.text: Client Script
UI Policy
Script Include
Notification

questions.explanation: Script Includes provide a single location for reusable functions, reducing maintenance and time-to-completion.

questions.prompt: The "Auto map matching fields" utility can map fields automatically under which condition?

choices.text: When the source field names match the target field names
When the target table extends the Task table
When the import set contains exactly two columns
When the source file is provided in CSV format with a defined header row

questions.explanation: Auto map matching fields works when the import-set field names are identical to the target-table field names; one click then creates the field maps. Any mismatches can be corrected afterward with the Mapping Assist utility.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the 'Override application menu roles' option on a module?

choices.text: It lets users open the module even without access to the containing menu, subject to the module's own roles.
It removes all role requirements from the module entirely
It hides the module from the application menu entirely, but keeps it accessible only through a direct URL.
It grants the module's roles to the parent application menu

questions.explanation: Override application menu roles allows a user to open the module even if they cannot see the containing menu. The user must still satisfy the module's own Roles requirement.

questions.prompt: Why should the 'Ignore cache' checkbox be selected on application properties?

choices.text: To improve runtime performance by caching the property's value indefinitely across requests.
To ensure the application uses the current property value rather than a cached one.
To prevent admins from editing the property.
To allow the property to be a reference field.

questions.explanation: Ignore cache ensures the app reads the current property value instead of a cached value, so changes take effect immediately.
